(BY SRI B.N.JAGADEESHA, ADDL.SPP FOR R-1;
 SRI SUBHASH R., ADVOCATE FOR R-2)

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C.,(528 OF BNSS) PRAYING TO ALLOW THE PETITION BY QUASH THE PROCEEDINGS IN CR.NO.76/2022 REGISTERED BY UPPARPET P.S BENGALURU PENDING ON THE FILE OF HON'BLE 5TH A.C.M.M AT BENGALURU IN C.C.NO.32072/2022 FOR THE OFFENCES P/U/S 498-A, 323, 504, 506 OF IPC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.32072/2022, pending before the 5th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 323 of the IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 in unison submit that the parties to the lis during the pendency of the proceedings before this Court, have settled their dispute amicably and decided to live together happily.
An application NC: 2024:KHC:51060 under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C., along with the affidavits of both the parties are also filed before this Court to that effect.

3. The application under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C., reads as follows:
"1.

It is submitted that, the Respondent No.2 is the de- facto complainant in Crime No.76/2022 registered by Upparpet Station against the Petitioner and other accused for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code 1860, Pursuant to the same chargesheet is filed pending on the file of Hon'ble 5th Addl Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru in CC.No.32072/2022.
The Petitioner has filed the above petition being aggrieved by the proceedings in CC.No.32072/2022 and the chargesheet filed therein.

2. The Petitioner submits that, the present proceedings was arising out of the matrimonial differences between the Petitioner and the Respondent No.2, on the Lakshmaiah K vs State Of Karnataka on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112745756/

3. The Petitioner submits that, the Respondent No. 2 does not have any objections to this Application being allowed by this Hon'ble Court and as is forthcoming in the affidavit filed by the Respondent No. 2.

4. The Petitioner submits that, the Petitioner and the Respondent No.2 have out of their own free will, volition and consent without any coercion or any other influence,
decided to join each other and lead a matrimonial life and therefore, this application is filed.
5. The Petitioner submits that, the offences charged in the impugned proceedings are compoundable by this Hon'ble Court.

NC: 2024:KHC:51060 Wherefore, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to compound the offences charged against the Petitioner in Crime No.76/2022,
registered by Upparpet Police Station Bengaluru, pending on the file of Hon'ble 5th Addl Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru in CC.No.32072/2022, for the offences punishable under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506, of Indian Penal Code 1860,
in the interest of justice."

sentences.text: In the light of the fact that the dispute revolves around the husband and the wife; the parties have arrived at settlement and now the couple are living together happily, I deem it appropriate to accept the application and the affidavits and terminate the proceedings against the petitioner, as the allegations are not against the State.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The criminal petition is disposed.
(ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.32072/2022, pending before the 5th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stand quashed.
